chapter: Technique, jam sessions, audiences and records
title: Jack Teagarden jamming with the band
summary: Jack Teagarden often came to all-night horn-and-piano jams with the band and learned riffs from the players.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah, there sure were. All of them. Back in them days, all them would come around... Jack Teagarden and all them, we used to meet them and jam all night. Go out in one of them good-time houses where we'd just set a piano out there and play... Because they already had piano anyway. Take a piano player out there and play all night. We didn't have to have no drums or nothin'. Just the horns.
Yeah, the horns and piano, and jamming (?) on. Jack was pattin' their foot loud enough to keep time.
What about Charlie Teagarden? Did he come out too?
No. I don't remember him coming down. But Jack went and hung around us all the time.
Charlie was younger. Maybe he was too young.

Yeah. He hardly talked about his brother. But Jack loved that "St. Louis Blues," and he wanted to learn a lot of stuff behind it. "St. Louis Blues." He learned a lot from them guys playing, all of the different trumpet players and trombone players, and the saxophone players, and all of them playing clear, and all of them be out there jamming around, and he learned a lot of stuff, riffs and things, you know. The guys make different kinds of runs and things. He learned a lot of things.
When he first started coming out to sit in with you, was his style not yet formed?
Mmm-hmm. Yeah, he was playing just like...
Oh yes. He was playing in one of them big bands down at a hotel downtown.
